F1_arm_WLS_flatprior.question: How much of WLS's advantage over GENCO comes from the generator-limit dispatch prior? Make the prior carry no generator-specific information, exactly as GENCO's A1 arm does, and rerun.
F1_arm_WLS_flatprior.definition: Identical to the published arm (same scenarios, masks, seeds, noise, solver (8,12) LM iterations, DC-angle start, sigma continuation, priors on Q, weak |V| prior, metric) EXCEPT the generator active-power limits entering the P prior (and therefore also the DC-angle start, which is built from p_pri): for every in-service generator of a scenario, Pmax := median of Pmax over that scenario's in-service generators (one value for all of them), Pmin := 0. Bus-level Pmin/Pmax are then sums over the generators at the bus, as before. So s = clip((1.02*sum(Pd) - 0)/(sum Pmax_flat - 0),0,1), the P prior at a bus is n_gens_at_bus * s * Pmax_median minus the bus load, and sigma_P = max(n_gens_at_bus*Pmax_median/2, 10 MW)/100 (an equal-share, wide prior). Q limits (Qmin/Qmax) are LEFT as published, because GENCO's A1 leaves Qg limits and voltage limits untouched; WLS uses no cost coefficients so A2 has no WLS counterpart.
F1_arm_WLS_flatprior.matches: tracks/genco-challenge/results/2026-10-22-genco-voltage-limit-ablation/protocol.json arm A1_nolimits: 'Pmax := median of the Pmax values of that scenario's in-service generators (same value for every generator), Pmin := 0'. That protocol file was read before this amendment.
F1_arm_WLS_flatprior.sets_and_order: 40% measured buses, noise-free, configs f40_s0..2, in this order: (1) 36 carved datakit pieces (control + family-vs-size, the ablation's 'pieces' set), first 30 scenarios of each test list; (2) locked-15 grids, f40_s0 (the only 40% config of that study) then f20_s0..2, first 30 scenarios; (3) the 15 seen-family whole grids, first 10 scenarios; (4) the 17 unseen-family whole grids, first 10 scenarios; (5) EXTRA, only if time remains: 36 ladder-generated pieces (generator-control), first 30 scenarios, f40. Within a set, grids run smallest first (by the published WLS wall time). 10% and noisy configurations are not run for the flat prior.
F1_arm_WLS_flatprior.comparisons_preregistered: Per cell, with the same bootstrap draws as the published cells (rng seeded by crc32(study|grid|cond), 2000 resamples, win = point ratio<1 and 95% CI upper<1, best comparator re-selected inside each resample): (i) 'info-asymmetric': GENCO as released vs best(I1-I5, W_flat); (ii) 'flat both sides': GENCO-A1 (limits made uninformative, read from 2026-10-22-genco-voltage-limit-ablation/per_grid/genco_ablate_<grid>.jsonl, arm A1, configs f40_s0..2, subset to the same first-k scenarios) vs best(I1-I5, W_flat); also (iii) GENCO-A1 vs W_flat alone and GENCO vs W_flat alone, reported as both 'GENCO significantly better' (ratio<1, CI upper<1) and 'WLS significantly better' (ratio>1, CI lower>1). Cells where the A1 file is missing/incomplete are reported as 'flat-both-sides not available', never imputed. Interpolators are I1-I5 as stored (they have no access to generator limits).
F1_arm_WLS_flatprior.fallback_variant: Same as published: non-converged scenarios replaced by the I2 error, reported next to the primary.

Run on the 15 seen-family whole grids at 40% (f40_s0..2), first 10 scenarios (the same subset as the published oos run), ascending by size, after the flatprior sets above, as far as time allows before the 07:15 EDT compute stop. A grid enters the table only if all three seeds completed.
